"Um. It's written on the equipment cases. See, here. It says 'property of the Galatia Academy Planetology Department by the authority of Academician Cornelius Elek..." their words drift off as results start to come in.

Academician Cornelius Elek. A somewhat self-important man, as you recall. You received a message from him about some mission to the fringe - and rejected his offer.

It seems you have inadvertently discovered what he was asking you to find.

"$PlayerSirOrMadam." They tap a few commands and release a data-packet from the isolated computing environment to your personal datapad.

You have the coordinates for... something. Something that someone thought was important 200 cycles in the past. And that Cornelius Elek thought was important much more recently.

You could either go in blind to find out what's out there, or go to the Galatia Academy to see if Academician Elek is open to revisiting the terms of his proposal.

"$PlayerSirOrMadam." They tap a few commands and release a data-packet from the isolated computing environment to your personal datapad.

You have the coordinates for... something. Something that someone thought was important 200 cycles in the past. And that Cornelius Elek thought was important much more recently.

Considering how thoroughly you burned your bridges with Academician Elek, there's only one way to find out what's out there...

Who cares about some academician's speculation? Their perspective is limited to the walls of that ivory torus orbiting a gas giant in the Galatia System.

You may simply strike at the heart of this mystery.

"I'm not available for questions right now," he says, cutting you off.

"Office hours are in the syllabus provided by my teaching assistant. Please visit my office at an appropriate time, thank-you and goodbye."

He hits the comms cut-off.

"I'm not available right now," he says without looking up. "Office hours are in the syllabus, good-bye."

He hits the comms cut-off.

Perhaps an in-person visit will force him to listen to you.

Elek begins to say something, and fails. He rubs his hands together nervously.

"I... I see. Yes, you're probably... it's very..."

He trails off, staring into space. He looks sad and a little bit confused. Without looking at you, he begins to speak again.

His eyes widen. "Truly? That is to say, marvelous! I did not take you for a champion of science, but you may yet force me to re-evaluate my first impression."

Elek smiles, and seems to mean it.

The comms take a moment to connect.

"I'm very busy," says Elek. You can see the back of his head as he configures something on a secondary interface. "Out with it, please, whoever you are."
OR
After a moment, the comms flicker into a stable connection.

Elek's attention appears to be focused on his datapad, but he sighs deeply, then sullenly drops it onto his desk. "Is the comms buffer insufficient for your purposes? I hope your communication proves informative."

After a moment the comms connect.

"Yes?" A holographic planetoid whizzes past Elek's head. "Did we not just speak? I'm in the middle of calibrating my model."

The comms flicker and hold. K-O Jove watches you with a wisp of smile, as if amused; as if assessing you like a prize.

"Captain," he says.

The comms flicker and hold. K-O Jove watches you with a wisp of smile, as if amused; as if assessing you like a prize.

"Captain," he says. "Have you brought me my 100,000 credits?"

Your TriPad pings confirmation as Jove nods, a slow smile growing on his face.

"Thank you. There's so little trust in these worlds, I am grateful to count upon you to pay your due."

He blinks, slowly, and releases a breath.

"Pity," he says. Then waves you away. "Get to it, yes?"

The comms cut, leaving you with a blank feed.

Jove sighs, disappointed. 

"Lie, captain, but not to me. You know better."

He pulls his feet off from where he had them propped up, then sits up straight.

Jove looks through the feed.

"Let me make quite sure of this because it would be beneath me to take your declaration lightly. Tell me, captain, is it true you intend to break our sacred trust?"

His tone is peculiar. Like some yawning depth lies beneath his pretty words.
"You've a poor sense of wit," Jove says coldly. "I suggest you refrain from attempting its use."

"I see," he says quietly, bowing his head as if in pain.

"Good-bye." Almost a whisper.

The feed cuts abruptly to black.

"Welcome to Nomios, Captain $playerLastName."

$personName's voice is suffocatingly calm.

"How can Mbaye-Gogol assist you on your journey?"

"Welcome to Nomios, Captain $playerLastName."

$personName's voice is suffocatingly calm.

"Ah, I see you bear a commission from our friends at Tri-Tachyon. How can Mbaye-Gogol assist you on your journey?"

"Welcome back to Nomios, Captain $PlayerLastName."

$personName's voice is as calm as asphyxiation.

"Captain $PlayerLastName. I'm sure we would not wish to waste any of your time here on Nomios."

$personName's voice is as calm as asphyxiation.
He nods slowly, unblinking.

Gallu Blanc's smile couldn't thaw ice-phase hydrogen.

"I am pleased to hear of your interest. Although I do not usually deal directly with clients, I do take pleasure in facilitating services for certain... exceptional individuals."

"And although you are not insignificant, captain," his tone is magnanimity itself, "-please take no offense, but I must inquire about your financial situation. We offer something approaching immortality and its price... is dear."

Gallu Blanc's eyebrows raise minutely as he reviews your financial data.

"Impressive," he says. "This gives us much leeway in terms of the highly exclusive, cutting-edge services that Mbaye-Gogol can offer to its best clients."

You put on a good act as an impatient independent warlord who has more a mind for strategy and tactics than the details of record-keeping and accounts, feigning annoyance at your purser as they 'struggle' to assemble the requested data.

In fact, your officers begin to assemble a falsified list of gray and black-market holdings, many associated with known criminal syndicates and pirate gangs. It's the sort of portfolio that would send both a Hegemony inspector and a Luddic curate into a rage, one that is difficult to quickly verify, but also one which would be quite plausible for a successful individual in your position.

Gallu Blanc bears your show of middling competence patiently, and nods politely when the files are finally submitted.

"You have a very... diverse portfolio, captain," he says mildly. "Properly utilized... well, in any event, this gives us a great deal of leeway in terms of accessing the highly exclusive, cutting-edge services that Mbaye-Gogol offers only to its best clients."

Gallu Blanc's eyebrows raise minutely as he reviews your financial data. It is perhaps the most human expression you've seen him make.

"You are too humble by half, captain," he says. "You have over a million credits in your accounts. This gives us much leeway in terms of the highly exclusive, cutting-edge services that Mbaye-Gogol can offer to its best clients."

"Not insubstantial," he concedes.

"That may open up some," he emphasizes that word, "possibilities for some of the more exclusive services Mbaye-Gogol offers to its better clients."

"I understand that you've a very active career," he says with the patience of the interstellar medium.

"I wish you good fortune. Perhaps we may discuss these matters again before long?"

"Of course, captain," he says with the patience of the interstellar medium. "I assure you that Mbaye-Gogol is committed to your absolute privacy in all matters. Our reputation spans generations, after all."

"I understand that you've a very active career. Perhaps it is premature to discuss these matters before you feel prepared to commit to trusting our timeless institution."

"Your enthusiasm is most compelling, but we always put the client first."

He produces a pained little smile, like a vacuum-dessicated corpse.

"I couldn't waste any more of your valuable time, captain," he says. "I wish you profitable ventures."

He cuts the comms.

He folds his hands together.

"How may the Mbaye-Gogol Cryosanctum assist you in your journey through time?"

Gallu Blanc's smile couldn't thaw ice-phase hydrogen.

"Although I do not usually deal directly with clients, I take pleasure in facilitating services for exceptional individuals."

He nods minutely, a glacial magnanimity.

"How may the Mbaye-Gogol Cryosanctum assist you in your journey through time?"

You explain your requirements in somewhat elliptical terms. It is a politically and ethically sensitive proposal, after all.

As Blanc picks up on your intimations, he almost looks amused. "Hardly a unique case, $playerSirOrMadam."

"We welcome many guests with... unique medical situations to the Mbaye-Gogol Cryosanctum."

"May we suggest a secure, mid-term care package for 100,000 credits? It has a 50-cycle guarantee of integrity with very reasonable rewewal options."

"I believe I recall the details of the situation," Blanc says, stone-faced.

"May we suggest a secure, mid-term care package for 100,000 credits? It has a 50-cycle guarantee of integrity with very reasonable renewal options."

The arrangements are made.

An anonymous shuttle carries an unmarked cryosleep-unit into the bowels of Nomios. The telemetry from the subtle tracking device you had installed on the unit cuts off as soon as it is wheeled through the first set of doors.

Leonidas will be safe, here. And the Sector safe from Leonidas.

For now.

"Certainly."

Blanc's mouth arranges itself into something he was probably told looked pleasant.

He makes a subtle motion, and a form appears in the comms-link. A list of packages. You skim the text - various levels of insurance, guarantees, bodily integrity maintained... regrowth of damaged elements upon thawing, neural integrity treatments...

"I'm not sure this is the right choice for you, captain. But," he lays a patient expression over his disapproval, "perhaps we may establish a... baseline."

"The budget option discards most of the unnecessary appendages, and indeed most of the corpus itself. These components help offset the expense of offering such a... reasonable option, you see."

"Not exactly," he says, blandly correcting you. "The procedure is quite controlled, and retains a reasonable portion of the spinal cord to ease reconstruction."

A pause.

"It was also found that the standard cryocephalic unit permits the storage of certain... additional small organs considered by some to have sentimental value, as well. A popular option."

"Of course," he says with the mildest disapproval. "A common option for... those of limited means."

"Much of the body is preserved, though to fit the smaller, and more efficient, long-term cryo units, certain reversible procedures are undergone to remove as much unnecessary volume and mass as possible."

He smiles icily. 

"The commonplace organs are removed - to bring down the cost of cryosanctum, you see. And then, much of the fat, muscle, and bones are..."

Blanc licks his lips. You'd swear his tongue makes a rasping sound, but that may simply have been signal interference. 

"Think of it as... folding. Folding was an ancient art on Old Earth, I am told," he muses. "The resulting package is quite compact, retaining all the distinctive elements of mind and body, to be... reconstructed at a future date."
